title: Truth Seeker - Axis of distortion
description: A group of friends in wartime St. Pölten race to find Elli’s arrested fiancé before he vanishes into the Nazi detention system. Following a trail of forged documents, patrol maps, and encoded ciphers, they push deeper into a web of danger and deception—where every clue uncovers new risks, and every decision could change his fate. What awaits them at the end of the trail remains uncertain
download_info: Download the game files as a PDF by clicking the button below. Print the document and set everything up as explained on the first page. During gameplay, you’ll use the pages in stages—taking only the ones you need at each moment. Once a page has served its purpose, you can discard it and continue with the next part.
rule_time_limit: You have 1 hour to complete the game.
rule_clues: If you get stuck, you can ask Elli for clues.
rule_diary: For data visualizations, you can always check your research diary.
rule_settings: Settings are available throughout the entire game.
intro_text: In 1938, Nazi Germany annexed Austria and erased its independence. Austrian institutions, culture, and political opposition were suppressed as the Nazi regime transformed the country into part of the German Reich. What followed was years of war, fear, and destruction across Europe.
intro_text2: Now, in April 1945, the Third Reich is collapsing. The Soviet Red Army are advancing from the east while the US Army push forward from the west. Air raids strike towns and cities throughout Austria, including St. Pölten, a city in the Reichsgau Niederdonau between Vienna and Linz. The Nazi administration is in chaos, and many officials are desperately trying to flee before the Allies arrive.
intro_text3: As another bombing raid forces you into the damp cellars beneath the city, you receive a message from your friend Elli. She urgently asks you and your friends to meet at your apartment as soon as the attack is over.
intro_text4: Your apartment is strangely quiet. Despite the destruction around the city, the building itself appears mostly untouched. You wait for Elli and her fiancé, who have lived in the city for nearly two years.
intro_text5: Standing in the courtyard, you finally find Elli. Shaken and terrified, she explains that two men arrived shortly before sunrise to arrest both her and her fiancé. While Elli managed to hide, her fiancé was taken away.
intro_text6: In their haste, the men left several documents behind in the apartment. Elli took these documents with her.
intro_text7: Perhaps these papers contain clues about who took him — and why.
story1_text: After the incident report, the pressure on Elli and the players rises. Her fiancé has been taken, and no one knows where he will be brought next or whether they can reach him in time.
story1_text2: The apartment is no longer safe. The regime enforcers could return at any moment. If they do, they might take the whole group. Staying is not an option anymore.
story1_text3: Elli tries to stay calm, but fear is written across her face
story1_text4: “We have to leave,” she says quietly. “For good.”
story1_text5: She explains that even within the equally aligned people, the safe house is kept secret. Only a few selected members know its location and password. Her fiancé was one of them.
story1_text6: The safe house may be their only chance, but Elli does not know where it is. She remembers that her fiancé kept important documents in his office, documents that might contain the location and the password.
story1_text7: The group searches quickly. Drawers are opened, papers are scattered, and every sound outside the door feels dangerous.
story1_text8: Finally, among the documents, they find something promising. It may be the clue they need to reach the safe house and continue the search for Elli’s fiancé.
story2_text: Once the briefcase is finally opened, you discover that it contains far more than ordinary government paperwork. Inside are forged passports, ration cards, coded messages, and lists of names carefully hidden between official documents.
story2_text1: Elli quickly searches through the files while the others keep watch near the windows. It soon becomes clear that the documents belonged to a network of people working against the Nazi regime.
story2_text2: Some files describe students distributing anti-war leaflets and secretly copying forbidden radio broadcasts. Many of the documents describe how information was secretly gathered and passed on. Resistance members of all kind listened to foreign radio stations, copied military movements, forged identity papers, and used coded letters to communicate between safe houses.
story2_text3: Among the files, Elli suddenly discovers a large Sankey diagram marked with official stamps and handwritten notes.
story3_text: After uncovering the discrepancy in the Sankey chart, Elli grows increasingly uneasy. The list of missing detainees includes several political prisoners — and her fiancé had already been marked as one of them.
story3_text1: Unable to ignore the discovery, she immediately begins searching through the remaining documents stored inside the safe, hoping to uncover what happened to the missing prisoners.
story3_text2: Among the official reports and transport records, one item stands out: a carefully folded letter hidden between the files.
story3_text3: Unlike the other documents, it is not written in plain text.
final_story: Now you finally know where Elli’s fiancé was supposed to be taken: Mauthausen. The concentration camp in Upper Austria is infamous for imprisoning political opponents, resistance members, and prisoners from across occupied Europe. Neither you nor Elli are willing to wait any longer. If there is still a chance that he is alive, you must reach Mauthausen as quickly as possible.
final_story1: On the journey west, you manage to arrange a ride with a Soviet convoy heading toward the Danube. Among other people in the back of the GAZ-AA truck, you and Elli travel alongside exhausted Red Army soldiers moving through the devastated countryside.
final_story2: Contrary to the rumours spread during the war, the young Soviet soldier driving the truck seems friendly. He appears almost relieved to speak with local teenagers instead of fellow soldiers.
final_story3: He agrees to take you as far as Emmersdorf an der Donau, a small village near Krems. Here  begins the American occupation zone. From there, you continue by foot along the northern bank of the Danube, heading toward Mauthausen.
final_story4: When you finally arrive, the area around the camp is heavily guarded. Soldiers patrol the roads while trucks and medical vehicles move in and out through the gates. As you get closer, you realize these are not German troops.
final_story5: The uniforms belong to American G.I.s. The Americans must have advanced rapidly through Upper Austria and reached Mauthausen before your arrival.
final_story6: One of the soldiers’ steps forward and asks Elli why you have come. With a trembling voice, she explains everything: the arrest of her fiancé, the documents left behind in St. Pölten, the journey to the safe house, and the evidence suggesting he had been brought to Mauthausen. The soldier silently searches through several lists before slowly looking back up at her.
final_story7: “I’m sorry, ma’am,” he says quietly. “Your fiancé’s name isn’t among the prisoners we found after liberating the camp.”
final_story8: He hesitates for a moment before continuing.
final_story9: “We still don’t know what happened to many of the detainees. I can’t tell you whether he died here, or if he ever reached the camp at all. For what it’s worth, I am sorry for your loss.”
puzzle1_story: As you search the dark briefcase, Elli goes still.
puzzle1_story2: “That’s theirs,” she whispers. “The uniformed men must have left it behind.”
puzzle1_story3: Inside, you find stamped reports, maps, and charts. Elli spreads them across the desk, her eyes scanning the pages quickly. She figures that both her fiancé and she are wanted by the Nazi officials for looting bombed houses and “insidious attacks on the state, the party or party uniforms”.
puzzle1_story4: “Preposterous! These allegations are completely false! We’ve never…”. Elli stops.
puzzle1_story5: “Here are security reports,” she says. “They list incidents across the district over several weeks… maybe this is why they took my fiancé.”
puzzle1_story6: One report catches her attention: a line chart split across two graphs, followed by documents naming different locations in the district.
puzzle1_story7: “We need to understand what really happened. Check the chart carefully, find the date with the highest incident activity, then we can find out where the most incidents happened on that day.”
puzzle2_story: Among ordinary files and paperwork, two items immediately catch your attention: a detailed map of central St. Pölten and a bundle of documents hastily stapled together.
puzzle2_story2: The papers appear to contain patrol schedules, checkpoints, and movement orders left behind by Nazi officials. The map itself seems recently updated, with several streets and buildings marked by hand.
puzzle2_story3: She points toward several markings on the map.
puzzle2_story4: “The city is being heavily watched,” she whispers. “If we want to survive, we need to find a safe route to the safe house in the northwest of St. Pölten.”
puzzle2_story5: Elli lowers her voice as she looks toward back at the table.
puzzle2_story6: “Maybe these patrol documents can help us avoid the checkpoints.”
puzzle3_story: After successfully reaching the safe route through the city, Elli looks at the entrance in silence before speaking again.
puzzle3_story1: “Reaching the safe house doesn’t help us if we can’t get inside,” she says. “The building is usually guarded. Only trusted people know the password.”
puzzle3_story2: She searches nervously through the remaining papers.
puzzle3_story3: “My fiancé never wrote the password down directly. It would have been too dangerous.” She carefully takes a propaganda sheet out of her pocket.
puzzle3_story4: “I think this was their way of hiding the information. I’ve seen this before. It is a British propaganda pamphlet. They are easy to get, and the Nazi’s would never suspect this to contain the password”
puzzle3_story5: Elli gives the paper to you.
puzzle3_story6: “Whatever the password is, it must be hidden somewhere in this poster”
puzzle3_story7: As you approach the safe house, a dark figure approaches you. “Greetings. I’m certain you look for accommodation this evening. To go further you must give me the following information:
puzzle4_story: BRITAIN 1945 – BLUE - VICTORY! That sounds about right. Once you and Elli reach the safe house and enter using the correct code word, they are welcomed by other members already hiding there. There you get some rest and keep watch, as the war around St. Pölten intensifies. Going outside now is too dangerous as the Red Army now advances westwards.
puzzle4_story1: The safe house offers temporary shelter and a chance to regroup, but it also brings a new opportunity. The group inside explains that they recently recovered a locked briefcase from the ruins of a government building that had been struck during an air raid. The briefcase is believed to have belonged to an official of the regime, which makes it a promising source of information. Alongside it, they found a note that may have belonged to the same person and could contain the numbers needed to open it. The friends in the safe house tried to figure out the code but failed.
puzzle5_story: Once the briefcase is open, you are presented with a lot of documents, passports and other technical objects. You and Elli immediately try to search the documents. While you find a Sankey-Diagram, Elli finds a censored letter and additional files. Now you must figure out when and where to Ellis Fiancé was deported. The chart does not contain names but shows how groups of detainees were transported from St. Pölten westwards with Mauthausen as the potential destination.
puzzle5_story1: From the earlier incident report, the group already knows that Elli’s fiancé was classified as a political prisoner. That makes the discrepancy especially significant. For Elli, that makes the chart impossible to ignore. The urge to find out who those political prisoners were is too strong, and she immediately begins checking the other papers in the safe for anything that might name them or explain where they were taken.
puzzle6_story: The letter is encrypted using an Enigma machine, its message locked behind shifting settings that must be carefully calibrated before any meaning can be extracted.Elli studies the attached documents and notices that they contain numbers, letters, and Roman numerals. She explains that these elements are essential for setting up the machine correctly:
puzzle6_story2: “These markings aren’t random—you’ll need them to calibrate the Enigma before you can even attempt to decrypt the letter.”
puzzle6_story3: She makes a connection to the earlier snakey record, pointing out that one of the documents matches it in structure:
puzzle6_story4: “This is the document you need, it has the exact same number of people as from the snakey.”
puzzle6_story5: Elli then recognizes the name Elias Richter on one of the files, her husband. The document shows he was sent somewhere, but the location has been censored:
puzzle6_story6: “This is Elias Richter my husband. The document shows he was sent somewhere, but the location has been redacted.”
puzzle6_story7: She concludes that the encrypted letter may contain the missing information.

puzzle7_story: This is the decrypted letter from the Enigma.
info_text_left: This puzzle uses a data visualization. Look at patterns, axes, and relationships carefully.
info_text_left6:
A node graph shows how different things are connected to each other. It is made of: Nodes — the points or circles that represent people, places, systems, or objects. Links/Edges — the lines that show relationships or connections between the nodes. What it is good for: understanding relationships, finding patterns or groups, showing networks and connections. Easy way to think about it: a node graph is like a map of friendships or connections.

A flow map shows movement from one place to another. It combines a map with lines or arrows to display direction and amount of movement. What it is good for: showing travel or transportation, displaying migration or trade, explaining how something moves over time or space. Easy way to think about it: a flow map is like tracking where things go and how much moves between places.

A bar chart compares different categories using rectangular bars. The length or height of each bar represents a value. What it is good for: comparing numbers quickly, showing differences between groups, making data easy to read. Easy way to think about it: a bar chart is like a visual scoreboard for comparing amounts.
info_text_right6: The Enigma machine is a cipher device developed and used in the early- to mid-20th century to protect commercial, diplomatic, and military communication. It was employed extensively by Nazi Germany during World War II in all branches of the German military. The Enigma machine was considered so secure that it was used to encipher the most top-secret messages. The Enigma has an electromechanical rotor mechanism that scrambles the 26 letters of the Latin alphabet. In typical use, one person enters text on the Enigma's keyboard and another person writes down which of the 26 lights above the keyboard illuminated at each key press. If plain text is entered, the illuminated letters are the ciphertext. Entering ciphertext transforms it back into readable plaintext. The rotor mechanism changes the electrical connections between the keys and the lights with each keypress. In essence, the rotor's motion means every letter is encrypted with a different cryptographic key, making it highly resistant to conventional cryptographic attacks based on patterns the keys leave in the resulting ciphertext.
reveal1: First Clue: But something feels wrong. This line chart might have been falsified.
reveal2: Second Clue: Wait…do you see it? The y-axis is inverted. That changes everything.
reveal3: Solution: Wait… if the y-axis is inverted, the lowest point is actually the highest value. That means the 14th of April stands out.
reveal1.1: First Clue: Seems like we need to compare the patrol maps with the main map and mark the unsafe routes. Only then we can see which streets are safe.
reveal2.1: Second Clue: We need to find a route to the safe house that avoids every marked patrol path.
reveal3.1: Solution:  Mhm… one possible patrol path would be: Schubert Straße, Josef Straße, North - Schießstatt Promenade, North - Prater Straße and Continue North.
reveal1.2: First Clue: Try folding the paper first to reveal the missing pie chart.
reveal2.2: Second Clue: The missing chart is titled Britain 1945. Try folding it to get this result.
reveal3.2: Solution: The missing chart is titled Britain 1945 and shows 55% blue, seems like the word is Victory.
reveal1.3: First clue: First, put each data set in order from the smallest number to the largest. Then find the minimum and maximum. After that, look for the middle value, that is the median. Then split the data into a lower half and an upper half. The middle of the lower half is Q1, and the middle of the upper half is Q3. Draw the Boxplot with those values into the grid.
reveal2.3: Second clue: Now calculate K × I × F and D + A + P. Then subtract the second result from the first.
reveal3.3: Solution: I figured out the Result! It’s 6186.
reveal1.4: First Clue: Don’t read the diagram as separate labels — follow the flow from where the prisoners enter to where they leave.
reveal2.4: Second Clue: Look closely at Melk. Compare how many prisoners arrive there with how many leave through the two Melk routes.
reveal3.4: Solution: At Melk, 45 prisoners arrive but only 39 leave, meaning 6 are missing, and by matching the category symbols for Political Prisoners and Saboteurs, the missing six are identified as 3 Political Prisoners and 3 Saboteurs.
reveal1.5: First Clue: look which cities have the most reliable connections and have the most military machinery sent to them
reveal2.5: Second Clue: In all 3 documents the answers are connected same cities and units
reveal3.5: Solution:Correct answers in order- Roman numbers: I,II,IV; Letters: L, P, V; Numbers: 15, 16, 20
reveal1.6: First Clue: The names on the list and document match
reveal2.6: Second Clue: Connect each name on the document with a place
reveal3.6: Solution: He was sent to Mauthausen
puzzle2_start_elli: We need to reach the safe house on Goldegger Straße. Which way do we go?
puzzle2_schubert_elli: Mariazeller Straße goes south. Josef Straße runs north directly. Or we go via Maria Theresia Straße.
puzzle2_maria_elli: We can reach Josef Straße through Schul Ring or Kalcher Straße.
puzzle2_josef_elli: Linzer Straße branches off north-east. We can stay north toward Schießstatt Promenade.
puzzle2_schiessstatt_elli: Prater Straße goes north. Schießstatt Ring lies west. Brunn Gasse may be covered.
puzzle2_prater_elli: We are close. Cross Khittel Straße and enter Goldegger Straße.
puzzle2_ring_elli: Khittel Straße is ahead. Goldegger Straße is beyond the bridge.
puzzle2_success_elli: We made it. The safe house is ahead. No patrols.
puzzle2_success_text: Route confirmed. You and Elli reach the safe house.
